name: Can renovating an older home make it more comfortable and energy efficient?

mainEntity.name: Can renovating an older home make it more comfortable and energy efficient?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older-home remodeling can improve comfort and efficiency, but the best measures depend on the building envelope and existing systems. Context: sealing leaks, improving insulation, correcting ventilation, upgrading windows, or replacing equipment may interact with moisture and indoor-air conditions. Key factors: roof and wall condition, window performance, ducting, ventilation, electrical capacity, and the order of work. Practical guidance: fix water-management problems before adding interior finishes or insulation. Ask the design team to identify which improvements should occur together and which can wait. Evaluate comfort and operating goals alongside appearance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but begin with moisture control, air leakage, insulation, ventilation, windows, and system capacity rather than replacing finishes alone. Ask which improvements should be coordinated so one upgrade does not conceal a building-envelope or indoor-air problem.
